rationale: Dual-licensed repository. The root LICENSE declares SPDX `MIT AND BUSL-1.1` (LICENSE:9) covering MEILI SAS 2019-2025. The Community Edition (default feature set, all standard crates: milli, meilisearch-types, index-scheduler community_edition, dump, file-store, etc.) is MIT-licensed and freely usable including commercial use (README.md:104-108, LICENSE-MIT full text). The Enterprise Edition modules — sharding, S3-streaming snapshots, network/index replication — are licensed under Business Source License 1.1 (LICENSE-EE), which permits only non-production use without a separate commercial agreement (LICENSE-EE:8-13) and is NOT an OSI-approved open-source license. These EE modules are plainly marked with BUSL-1.1 headers (crates/meilisearch-types/src/enterprise_edition/mod.rs:1-4, crates/index-scheduler/src/scheduler/enterprise_edition/mod.rs:1-4) and are gated behind the `enterprise` cargo feature; the community_edition.rs stubs return RequiresEnterpriseEdition errors (crates/index-scheduler/src/scheduler/community_edition.rs). Status is REVIEW, not PASS, because although the default community build is permissive MIT, the repository bundles BUSL-1.1-licensed code that prohibits production use of EE features without a commercial agreement, and the workspace Cargo.toml `license = "MIT"` field understates this. A human reviewer must confirm a consuming product compiles only the MIT Community Edition and never incorporates or enables the EE-gated modules (BUSL-1.1) without a commercial license.
